subject: Random effect levels - discrepancy between data and model

messages.author: 2504f1f1633f946f
messages.subject: Random effect levels - discrepancy between data and model
parts:
Dear nimble users, I have an issue with random effects.
Specifically, when I have a dataset with, say, 100 observations divided into 10 groups, and I add the group as a random effect, the model estimates 100 levels of the random effect, not only 10 (10 will contain values and 90 will be empty).

Here is the code. As you can see, while I simulated 10 different groups (called "site"), the model correctly estimates 10 parameters, but there are additional random effects wich are stored but full of NAs.

My questions are:
- Is this affecting parameter estimates?
- Is this affecting model compilation and running times?
- Is there a way to avoid the calculation of these "empty" parameters, or, at least to avoid saving them in the output?



library(nimble)

set.seed(123)

n <- 100 # Number of observations
nsites <- 10 # Number of groups

# Parameters
a <- 1 # Intercept
b <- 1 # Slope
sigma <- 1 # Residual standard deviation
# Random effect
sigma.S <- 0.5 # Standard deviation of the site effect
S <- rnorm(nsites, 0, sigma.S) # 10 sites

# Assign each observation to a site
site <- sample(1:nsites, n, replace = T)

# Simulate data
x <- runif(n, -2, 2) # Covariate values
y <- a + b * x + S[site] + rnorm(n, mean = 0, sd = sigma)

plot(x, y)

# Create data frame
tab <- data.frame(x = x, y = y, site = site)

# Model
model <- nimbleCode({
 
  for(i in 1:n){
   
    mu[i] <- a + b * x[i] + S[site[i]]
    y[i] ~ dnorm(mu[i], tau)
   
  }
  tau <- pow(sd,-2)
  sd ~ dunif(0, 10)
 
  ## Priors
  a ~ dnorm(0,0.01)
  b ~ dnorm(0,0.01)
  for(i in 1:nsites){ S[i] ~ dnorm(0, tau.S)}
  tau.S <- pow(sd.S,-2)
  sd.S ~ dunif(0, 10)
 
 
})

# Format the data
data <- list(y = tab$y)
constants  <- list(n = n, nsites = nsites, x = tab$x, site = tab$site)

# Parameters to monitor
params <- c("a","b","sd",paste0("S[",1:nsites,"]"))

# inits
inits <- list(a=0,b=0,sd.S=0.1,S=rnorm(constants$n,0,0.1),sd=1)

# MCMC
nc <- 3 # Number of chains
ni <- 4*10^3 # Number of iterations
nb <- ni*3/4 # Burn-in
nt <- (ni-nb)/1000 # Thinning (to sample a total of 1000 posteriors)

# nimble model
Rmodel <- nimbleModel(code = model, constants = constants, data = data, inits = inits)
Rmodel$initializeInfo()
# mcmc
conf <- configureMCMC(Rmodel, print = F)
conf$addMonitors(params)
Rmcmc <- buildMCMC(conf)
# Compile the model and MCMC algorithm
Cmodel <- compileNimble(Rmodel)
Cmcmc <- compileNimble(Rmcmc, project = Rmodel)

# RUN THE MODEL
out <- runMCMC(mcmc = Cmcmc, niter = ni, nburnin = nb, nchains = nc, thin = nt, inits = inits, samplesAsCodaMCMC = T)

colnames(out$chain1)

MCMCvis::MCMCsummary(out, params = params, ISB=F)

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Random effect levels - discrepancy between data and model
parts:
Hi Mattia,
Thanks for the question. It looks like this is happening because your inits value for S has length 100. We'll have to look at why this is being carried forward to change the size of S in the compiled model and MCMC sample, but I believe the use of the model and the sampling should be correct.
HTH,
Perry

messages.subject: Re: Random effect levels - discrepancy between data and model
parts:
Hi Perry, thank you for your reply.

You are perfectly right! The issue was due to the inits of S.

To respond to the initial questions, I replicated the process in both ways (100 inits of S or 10), an these are the answers:
- Is this affecting parameter estimates?
Possibly. In some tirals S[1:10] and "a" did not rech convergence. Not sure about why.
- Is this affecting model compilation and running times?

It seems not. Running and compilation times seems to be similar 

Here is the code:

library(nimble)

set.seed(123)

n <- 1000 # Number of observations

nsites <- 10 # Number of groups

# Parameters
a <- 1 # Intercept
b <- 1 # Slope
sigma <- 1 # Residual standard deviation
# Random effect
sigma.S <- 0.5 # Standard deviation of the site effect
S <- rnorm(nsites, 0, sigma.S) # 10 sites

# Assign each observation to a site
site <- sample(1:nsites, n, replace = T)

# Simulate data
x <- runif(n, -2, 2) # Covariate values
y <- a + b * x + S[site] + rnorm(n, mean = 0, sd = sigma)

plot(x, y)

# Create data frame
tab <- data.frame(x = x, y = y, site = site)

# Model
model <- nimbleCode({
 
  for(i in 1:n){
   
    mu[i] <- a + b * x[i] + S[site[i]]
    y[i] ~ dnorm(mu[i], tau)
   
  }
  tau <- pow(sd,-2)
  sd ~ dunif(0, 10)
 
  ## Priors
  a ~ dnorm(0,0.01)
  b ~ dnorm(0,0.01)
  for(i in 1:nsites){ S[i] ~ dnorm(0, tau.S)}
  tau.S <- pow(sd.S,-2)
  sd.S ~ dunif(0, 10)
 
 
})

# Format the data
data <- list(y = tab$y)
constants  <- list(n = n, nsites = nsites, x = tab$x, site = tab$site)

# Parameters to monitor
params <- c("a","b","sd",paste0("S[",1:nsites,"]"))

# MCMC
nc <- 3 # Number of chains
ni <- 8*10^3 # Number of iterations

nb <- ni*3/4 # Burn-in
nt <- (ni-nb)/1000 # Thinning (to sample a total of 1000 posteriors)

## Wrong way:

# inits
inits <- list(a=a,b=b,sd.S=sigma.S,S=rnorm(constants$n,0,sigma.S),sd=sigma)
inits$S[1:10] <- S

t0 <- Sys.time()

# nimble model
Rmodel <- nimbleModel(code = model, constants = constants, data = data, inits = inits)
Rmodel$initializeInfo()
# mcmc
conf <- configureMCMC(Rmodel, print = F)
conf$addMonitors(params)
Rmcmc <- buildMCMC(conf)
# Compile the model and MCMC algorithm
Cmodel <- compileNimble(Rmodel)
Cmcmc <- compileNimble(Rmcmc, project = Rmodel)

# RUN THE MODEL

out1 <- runMCMC(mcmc = Cmcmc, niter = ni, nburnin = nb, nchains = nc, thin = nt, inits = inits, samplesAsCodaMCMC = T)
t1 <- Sys.time()

t_diff1 <- t1-t0

## Correct way
# inits
inits <- list(a=a,b=b,sd.S=sigma.S,S=S,sd=sigma)

t0 <- Sys.time()

# nimble model
Rmodel <- nimbleModel(code = model, constants = constants, data = data, inits = inits)
Rmodel$initializeInfo()
# mcmc
conf <- configureMCMC(Rmodel, print = F)
conf$addMonitors(params)
Rmcmc <- buildMCMC(conf)
# Compile the model and MCMC algorithm
Cmodel <- compileNimble(Rmodel)
Cmcmc <- compileNimble(Rmcmc, project = Rmodel)

# RUN THE MODEL

out2 <- runMCMC(mcmc = Cmcmc, niter = ni, nburnin = nb, nchains = nc, thin = nt, inits = inits, samplesAsCodaMCMC = T)
t1 <- Sys.time()

t_diff2 <- t1-t0

summ2 <- MCMCvis::MCMCsummary(out2)
summ1 <- MCMCvis::MCMCsummary(out1, params = rownames(summ2), ISB=F)

# Does this affect parameter estimates?
summ1;summ2

# And calculation times?
t_diff1;t_diff2
